test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A dealer marks his goods 10% above the cost price and allows 10% discount. What is his percentage gain or loss?
solution:
**Given:**

A dealer marks his goods 10% above the cost price and allows 10% discount.

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) - Discount

Marked Price (MP) = Cost Price (CP) × (1 + Markup Percentage)

Discount = MP × Discount Percentage

Gain or Loss Percentage = ((SP - CP) / CP) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let Cost Price (CP) = 100

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (1 + 10%)

⇒ MP = 100 × 1.1

⇒ MP = 110

Discount = MP × 10%

⇒ Discount = 110 × 0.1

⇒ Discount = 11

Selling Price (SP) = MP - Discount

⇒ SP = 110 - 11

⇒ SP = 99

Gain or Loss Percentage = ((SP - CP) / CP) × 100

⇒ Gain or Loss Percentage = ((99 - 100) / 100) × 100

⇒ Gain or Loss Percentage = (-1 / 100) × 100

⇒ Gain or Loss Percentage = -1%

**The dealer has a 1% loss.**
